text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been experiencing fever and altered mental state for the past two days. To begin our evaluation, are you experiencing any severe headache, neck stiffness, or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.

Based on your history of taking haloperidol, the presence of fever and altered mental status, and the absence of other infectious symptoms like headache or neck stiffness, the clinical picture strongly suggests Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I will now request specific lab results to confirm this diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: CBC, CMP, Creatine_Phosphokinase (CPK).
